title: The Waiting Truck
brief: At Meridian Foods it is 4:30 p.m. A truck is waiting to take 18 pallets of ready meals from batch RM-504 to a retail customer. The laboratory result for the batch is not yet available; it is expected at 7 p.m. The shift supervisor proposes releasing now "because results are always fine". Food safety requirements belong to the separate food safety system and are outside this visit. You have 12 visit points to decide and justify a response.

evidence.text: Release checklist for RM-504: laboratory result line is blank, but the "released" box is ticked by the supervisor at 4:20 p.m.
evidence.whyItMatters: Release must follow completion of the planned checks or an authorized decision.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read every line of the release checklist.

evidence.text: Release procedure RP-3 requires the laboratory result before release; exceptions need the technical manager and customer consent.
Laboratory: "Result at 7 p.m. We can't speed the test."
Past results: 2 of the last 50 batches failed the same test.
evidence.whyItMatters: "Always fine" is not supported by the data.

evidence.text: Supervisor: "Results are always fine. If we miss this truck we lose the slot. Just release it." (note 3)
evidence.whyItMatters: Leadership at every level must support release controls. Pressure must not replace verification.

evidence.text: Supervisor: "The technical manager can authorize exceptions and is on call."
Customer delivery window runs to 6 a.m. tomorrow.
evidence.whyItMatters: There is time to deliver after the result.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check how firm the deadline is.

evidence.text: Customer terms CT-2 forbid delivery before laboratory release without written consent.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer requirements on release must be met.

evidence.text: Driver: "I can come back at 8 p.m. or another truck can run at 9 p.m."
Noticeboard lists today's trucks in red.
evidence.whyItMatters: A dispatch plan is not a nonconformity.

evidence.text: Pallet labels for RM-504 show batch, date, and count.

decisions.prompt: What do you do at 4:35 p.m.?
options: Ask for the release tick to be withdrawn and the batch held, inform the technical manager, and arrange collection after the 7 p.m. result within the customer's window
decisions.rationale: The result is due well within the delivery window. Holding and rescheduling meets the requirement and the customer's need.
optionFeedback: This ships before verification and breaches customer terms.
Proportionate and meets both the control and the delivery window.
Silence leaves a known breach in place.
There is no evidence the batch is bad.

decisions.prompt: How do you answer "results are always fine"?
options: Point out calmly that 2 of the last 50 failed, and that the check exists for the batch that does not pass
Tell the supervisor they are wrong in front of the team
decisions.rationale: Facts, stated calmly, address the pressure without blame.

containment: Hold RM-504 and remove the release tick until the result is reviewed
correction: Release after a passing result, or follow the nonconforming product process if it fails
cause: The release checklist allows the release box to be ticked with a blank result line
corrective: Make the result a required field before release can be recorded, and plan dispatch slots after expected result times
effectiveness: Audit release checklists weekly for two months

debriefText.found: You held release and found a route within the delivery window.
debriefText.missed: Under pressure, check how firm the deadline really is.
debriefText.falseFinding: The dispatch board and correct labels are conforming.
